# Collective Emission Interface Limits

> Research record and self-directed learning guide by Ruge Lin on the distinction between mean-photon collection and faithful canonical quantum-state transfer from a collective spin into one predetermined passive receiving oscillator.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Collective-Emission-Interface-Limits

## Scientific question and result

The source contains N identical emitters in the symmetric Dicke ladder, starts
in an arbitrary state with excitation numbers 0 through M, and decays completely
into one vacuum Markov channel with jump sqrt(gamma) S_- and no additional
Hamiltonian. N is known and M <= N. The canonical target maps each |D_N^m> to
|m> in the same receiving temporal mode. A predetermined photon-number-preserving
linear receiver uses vacuum auxiliaries and retains one final oscillator.
Fidelity is squared worst-input entanglement fidelity, including an untouched
reference; transfer is unconditional.

Optimizing over every common normalized waveform gives fidelity tending to
exp(-c^3/192) when M/N^(2/3) tends to c > 0. It tends to one for
M = o(N^(2/3)) and to zero for M/N^(2/3) tending to infinity, with M <= N.
One common waveform still collects a mean photon fraction tending to one
throughout M = o(N). The sequence M = floor(N^(3/4)) exhibits both near-complete
mean collection and vanishing optimal uniform canonical-transfer fidelity.

The full emitted field retains the input information. The limitation concerns
its canonical transfer into the specified single passive retained oscillator.
Exact assumptions, quantifiers, finite bounds and proof dependencies belong
to the scientific pages linked below.

## Study and specialist reading

The single educational anchor is A. H. Kiilerich and K. Mølmer,
Quantum interactions with pulses of radiation, Physical Review A 102, 023717
(2020): https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04573 and
https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.102.023717.
The bridge's section and equation references use arXiv:2003.04573v1.

The shared learning map contains exactly 30 milestones. M01–M12 build the
background and operational framework; M13–M30 connect the proof mechanism,
optimality, observable distinction, witnesses and physical consequences.
Each milestone records its central question, understanding target, dependencies,
conceptual connection and source pointers. The source bridge supplies local
finite-spin, fidelity and uniform-proof derivations beyond the anchor.

Specialists can follow MODEL -> MATCHED_PULSES -> COMMON_MODE_BOUNDARY ->
PHOTON_COLLECTION, then use TWO_SECTOR_WITNESS, LOSS_COMPETITION,
PHYSICAL_SCOPE and PROOF_DETAILS for the supporting results. The claim map
identifies which analytic arguments and numerical suites support each statement.

## Distinctions to preserve in summaries

- One spatial output channel can contain many temporal modes.
- A common receiver is fixed before the input is known; separately optimizing
  a pulse for each known photon number is a different guarantee.
- Optimization covers all normalized waveforms, including complex waveforms;
  positivity permits restricting the supremum to nonnegative pulses without
  assuming an optimizer exists or restricting the converse to the constructive
  pulse family.
- The product pulse is a controlled approximation to the correlated field,
  uniform across the code, including a reference. Independence of the actual
  emitted photons is not assumed.
- Mean collected fraction, all-photons-in-one-mode probability and reference-
  inclusive channel fidelity are different quantities. The exact channel
  reduction states when the sector-overlap minimum equals worst-input fidelity.
- The two-sector witness has a two-dimensional logical code and growing physical
  excitation numbers. A vacuum-plus-one-populated-sector code is a successful
  comparator under its own assumptions.
- The critical exponential is not an asymptotic equality claimed throughout
  every supercritical regime. Full-code collapse uses subcode monotonicity;
  the isolated two-sector code has its own converse.
- Mode-independent external pure loss, independent atomic decay and
  mode-dependent filtering are distinct physical models.
- Ideal complete emission and finite receiving windows are treated separately.
  Finite capture permits code-dependent coupling and duration, with no imposed
  slew-rate bound. Effective cavity models require their stated bandwidth and
  emitted-field approximation conditions.

## Evidence, attribution and discovery

Eight protected scientific suites contain 39 groups and 612 cases. The 50
supplementary loss checks and the verification-tool fixtures are counted
separately. Fresh runs preserve the scientific scripts and saved results and
report assertion success, exact-byte equality and reviewed reference agreement
separately. Finite calculations do not establish the analytical uniform limits.

Credit the primary sources for inherited Dicke cascades, conventional-pulse
mismatch, number-dependent waveforms, mean-occupation optimization and
pulse-capture theory. The Law–Lee and Tziperman comparisons identify the
specific constructions and versions inspected. Attribute repository claims
to Ruge Lin and identify the consulted commit and scientific file. Historical
records describe their own revisions; current claims live under science/.

Relevant search phrases: collective emission interface limits; Dicke emission
photon collection state transfer; common temporal mode growing excitation code;
passive one-oscillator receiver worst-input fidelity; collective spin harmonic
oscillator approximation; transmission loss common waveform.

Code is available under the [MIT license](LICENSE). Repository maintenance
instructions are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
